text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.

- For the first time since joining the European Economic Area (EEA), Norway is refusing to adjust to EU standards. Brussels is demanding that Norway change the law allowing employers to pay lower payroll taxes in rural areas.
- Groceries in Oslo are around 40 percent more expensive than in other Nordic cities. Since Sweden and Finland joined the European Union in 1994/95 food prices have fallen sharply.
- An increasing number of people are getting married in church and 84.1 percent of parents choose a Christian baptism for their children. However, fewer youngsters go through confirmation in church.

- Opposition in the Labour Party against privatisation of state-owned telecommunications company Telenor is declining. Gunnar Halvorsen, the party's representative on parliament's industry committee, says privatising Telenor would increase its global competitiveness.
- Increasing demand for electricity in the Nordic market over the next few years will lead to higher prices and increased imports of coal, state-owned electricity producer Statkraft says.
